chunks: Ali ibn Isa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Muhammad Majiluwayh narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated to us, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Ilwan al-Kalbi, from Amr ibn Thabit, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, in

Paradise there is a tree from whose top come garments and from whose bottom come piebald horses, saddled and bridled, with wings. They do not defecate nor urinate. The friends of God ride them, and they fly with them in Paradise wherever they wish. Those who are below them say:
"O our Lord, what has brought Your servants to this honor?" God, exalted is His majesty, says:

"Indeed, they used to stand in prayer at night and not sleep, and they would fast during the day and not eat, and they would fight the enemy without cowardice, and they would give charity without stinginess."

key_terms.أولياء الله: Friends of God, those closest to Him through devotion
key_terms.الجنة: Paradise (Jannah), the eternal abode of the righteous
key_terms.الكرامة: Honor, dignity, a special distinction granted by God

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards of night prayer and fasting in Paradise according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) describes a magnificent tree in Paradise that produces garments from its top and winged piebald horses from its bottom. The friends of God ride these celestial horses freely through Paradise, and when those of lower rank ask God what deeds earned such honor, God explains it was their devotion to night prayer, fasting, jihad, and charity. This hadith, transmitted through the family chain of Zayd ibn Ali from his Imami forefathers, was delivered in the context of encouraging believers toward four comprehensive acts of worship that combine personal devotion to God with active service to others.

en.bilal-muhammad: `Ali b. `Isa (ra) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Muhammad Majiluwayh narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Abi `Abdillah narrated to us from his father from al-Husayn b. `Ilwan al-Kalbi from `Amr b. Thabit from Zayd b. `Ali from his father from his grandfather (as). He said: Amir al-Mu’minin `Ali b. Abi Talib (as) said: In Paradise

there is a tree with gems that come out of the top and black-and-white winged horses that come out of the bottom. The horses do not defecate, nor do they urinate. The friends of Allah will ride them, and by them, they will fly wherever they want in Paradise. Those lower than them will say:
“O our Lord! How did Your servants attain this nobility?”

So, Allah will say: “They would pray in the night and not sleep, and they would fast in the day and not eat, and they would fight the enemies without cowardice, and they would give in charity without stinginess.”
